subject: Celestia2b elevated 5xx window and remediation plan
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Celestia2b — elevated 5xx observed on streaming chat route

Hi Liam —

Quick note from ops: starting at ~09:02 PDT we observed an elevated rate of 5xx / timeout responses impacting calls to model=Celestia2b on the streaming /v1/chat/generate route for a subset of BrightCart traffic. The symptoms were increased 502/503 responses and occasional stalled streams (client sees no tokens for ~15s then a 5xx). We flagged this in our monitoring and opened an on-call bridge.

Scope we see:
- Affects ~6% of BrightCart requests routed to Celestia2b between 09:02–09:44 PDT.
- Higher incidence for sequences >2k tokens and when clients use prefix-caching enabled.
- No data exfiltration concerns — requests and inputs remained within your account boundary.

Immediate actions taken (so you have visibility):
- At 09:10 we temporarily enabled automatic fallback routing for your account from Celestia2b -> Celestia2b-quant (compatible quantized variant) to reduce error rate.
- At 09:16 we increased concurrency on the dedicated pool serving BrightCart to absorb spikes while we triaged.
- At 09:27 we disabled a recent kernel-level scheduling optimization that we suspected correlated with the failures.
- At 09:44 error rates returned to baseline after the above mitigations.

What we still need to do:
- Full root cause analysis (we have an active Jira RW-OPS-1842).
- Post-incident follow-up with patch/rollback plan and permanent guardrails.

I've attached a short sample error log and the bridge notes. Would you like us to proactively route all BrightCart traffic off Celestia2b for a 24-hour window while we complete the RCA, or do you prefer the current fallback behavior (only on failure)?

Apologies for the disruption — we know latency/availability is critical during your peak ingest windows. We will provide an ETA for the postmortem in our next update (aiming EOD tomorrow).

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0138

Attachments: celestia2b_error_sample.log (text), initial-ops-bridge-notes.pdf (pdf)

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the quick heads up.

A couple quick questions:
1) How many of our production requests were impacted (absolute RPS and percentage is fine)?
2) Can you confirm whether any inference results were truncated or only errors returned? We had two downstream jobs that retried and produced duplicate entries — want to quantify.
3) We'd prefer full routing off Celestia2b for the next 24 hours if that avoids inconsistent behavior. Please confirm.

Also — given this was during our morning processing window, we'll be asking for a credit for the impacted period if remediation isn't covered by your SLA.

Liam
Director of Platform Engineering | BrightCart
liam@brightcart.com

Hi Liam —

Thanks — quick answers inline and plan:

1) Impacted volume: roughly 6% of your requests to Celestia2b between 09:02–09:44 PDT. Absolute peak impacted was ~18 RPS (your account peak was ~300 RPS to that model). We'll include exact request/latency histograms in the postmortem.
2) Behavior: most affected calls returned immediate 502/503; a small fraction (~0.2% of total) produced truncated responses after client retries. We are compiling a dedup list for your ingestion pipeline so you can reconcile duplicates.
3) Routing: we've now set account-level pinning so that all BrightCart requests will route to Celestia2b-quant for the next 24 hours per your request. You should see only the quantized model for this window. We'll revert to normal routing after we validate the fix, unless you instruct otherwise.

Compensation: we're prepared to offer a one-time credit equivalent to 25% of your inferred usage during the impacted hour (09:00–10:00 PDT) — if that works for you we can fast-track the credit and include it in your next invoice. If you prefer a different arrangement I'll escalate to billing.

Next steps from our side:
- Ops is collecting core dumps and kernel traces from the affected workers; engineering is reproducing the failure in a staging parity cluster.
- We will deliver a preliminary RCA by EOD tomorrow (May 15) and a full postmortem with patch timeline within 72 hours.
- I'll share a short reconciliation CSV for the truncated/duplicate responses once we finish matching.

Appreciate the patience — we'll follow up as soon as we have the RCA.

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-05-15T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Celestia2b incident postmortem & permanent mitigations (RW-OPS-1842)

Hi Liam —

TL;DR: Root cause identified, fixes merged, and permanent mitigations scheduled. Summary below and links to the full postmortem and Jira.

What happened (summary):
- Root cause: a kernel-level scheduling path introduced in v1.7.3 of our inference runtime caused a rare race when handling large KV-cache invalidation for long-context sequences on Celestia2b. The race could lead to an unhandled exception in the request handler which surfaced as 502/503 responses.
- Why BrightCart saw it: your workload has a higher proportion of long contexts + prefix caching enabled, which exercised the failure mode more frequently.

Impact observed:
- Elevated 5xx between 09:02–09:44 PDT on 2028-05-14; peak impacted ~6% of Celestia2b traffic for BrightCart (peak ~18 RPS).
- Small number of truncated responses where client retries caused duplicate downstream entries; we provided a reconciliation CSV (attached).

Immediate remediation performed: 
- Disabled the new scheduling path in production (rolled back v1.7.3 behavior for affected pool).
- Account-level routing to Celestia2b-quant for BrightCart for 24 hours (per your confirmation).
- Hotfix: a guard was added to the request handler to avoid the uncaught exception; hotfix has been deployed and validated in staging and can be rolled to prod on your schedule.

Permanent fixes & timeline: 
- Engineering has merged a deterministic scheduler fix (PR RW/runtime#672) — targeted deploy to canary cluster 2028-05-18, full rollout pending post-canary verification (expected by 2028-05-21).
- Add guardrails: request-level circuit breaker for long-context workloads and enhanced telemetry to detect cache-invalidation anomalies (in planning, Q3).

Customer commitments:
- Credit: we will issue the agreed 25% credit for usage between 09:00–10:00 PDT on 2028-05-14; billing will post to your next invoice.
- Postmortem: full postmortem is available here: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/ops/postmortems/Celestia2b-RW-20280514
- Jira ticket for tracking: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-OPS-1842

Attachments: reconciliation-duplicates.csv (generated), postmortem-summary.pdf

If you'd like, we can set up a 30-minute bridge with engineering to walk through the technical details and timeline — propose Thu 2028-05-18 09:00 PDT or Fri 2028-05-19 11:00 PDT. Let me know what works.

Again — sincere apologies for the disruption. Please reach out directly if you need anything else.

— Rafael
